buildNow.brief:
WHY: #7 ruling 1 (https://github.com/johnhenry/chatterang/issues/7#issuecomment-5669950639) calls for a hidden worker supervised like a host: a HostHandle whose loss is render-process-gone or destroyed, respawned under a cap, and destroyed when idle.

What stands in the way on main:
- A Supervisor spawns in its constructor (supervisor.ts:570).
- Its dispose is terminal (:931-938).
- Its restart cap is per instance (:1323-1343).
- HostFleet builds its supervisors at boot (host-fleet.ts:111-129).
- WorkBroker already takes `condemnExecutor` (work-broker.ts:339) and `workerLost(executor)` (:800), and main.ts:443-446 says the worker is what needs them.

The transport choice follows ruling 1 and S1's measurement (the host envelope over a MessagePort; doc:196-204), so it is settled here as engineering: one Supervisor per worker life, whose senderId is the worker's REAL webContents.id, never an invented number (work-broker.ts:76-82).

SCOPE
Add `apps/desktop/src/bridge/worker-host.ts`, with no `electron` and no `node:` import (tests/layering.test.ts bridge guard :1095-1119) and injected timers.
- `createWorkerHost({ spawnWorker: () => { handle: HostHandle; senderId: number }, broker, timers, policy })`.
- Build a Supervisor only when the first unit runs. After `WORKER_IDLE_MS` with no unit, call `dispose()` and drop it; the next unit builds a new one.
- Keep a restart budget ACROSS lives (maxRestarts / restartWindowMs), so recreating the Supervisor on admission cannot reset the cap.
- `run(unitId, encodedTurn, signal, onFrame): Promise<terminal>` runs one unit at a time. Abort calls the stream's cancel method.
- `condemn(executor): boolean` returns true only after the worker is killed, then calls `broker.workerLost(WORKER_EXECUTOR)`.
- `hostedUnitOf(senderId)`, for admitLocalTurns (local-turns.ts:157-188), answers only while that worker's unit runs.
- Export `WORKER_IDLE_MS` and `WORKER_EXECUTOR = 'worker'`.
- In protocol.ts, add a `PeerTurn` PluginDefinition and stream spec that pass the Supervisor's name check (supervisor.ts:516-545): methods `peerTurnStart` and `peerTurnCancel`; events `peerTurnFrame` (progress) and `peerTurnEnd` (terminal). buildNow.name: BN7 Paired-device registry file: verification data only, shared by both hosts
conflictsWith: BN6 (host/index.ts exports and HOST_EXPORTS rows; land after BN6)
buildNow.brief:
WHY: the only CredentialStore today is `createMemoryCredentialStore`, which forgets everything on exit (host/credential.ts:261-275). The #133 owner ruling (https://github.com/johnhenry/chatterang/issues/133#issuecomment-5670024680) puts the desktop's list in an app-data file next to the key: owner-only, sealed where available, holding what verification and revocation need and never the credential, and allowed to land tested but unreachable.

The server keeps the same records under --root (#124), and #158 wants one implementation. So the store lives beside identity-store.ts and takes its injectables: `KeyFileSystem` and `KeySealer` (identity-store.ts:156, :166) plus the same permission checks.

Settled here as engineering inside the rulings:
- Each record holds a digest or zero-byte tombstone, a name, and pairedAt. No lastSeenAt: it is neither verification nor revocation data.
- The store is BOUND to a 32-byte `bindTo` value. The desktop passes the tunnel key pin; the server passes a digest over the pin and its operator token (#135: the token is the root).
- A different bindTo at open clears every device and reports `cleared: 'binding-changed'` (#180: a key reset makes every device re-pair; #179: a Linux downgrade makes a new key and devices re-pair).
- A protection mismatch in the registry file itself is refused, never rewritten (the identity-store rule).

SCOPE
- `openDeviceRegistry({ directory, fs, sealer, bindTo, platform })` returns `{ store: CredentialStore; list(): DeviceRecord[]; setName(id, name); cleared: null | 'binding-changed' }`.
- `store` satisfies credential.ts:77-91 including the TOMBSTONE, and plugs into `createDeviceCredentials`.
- File format: a versioned envelope ('chatterang-paired-devices', v1) recording protection. Writes are atomic (temp file then rename) and serialised. The directory is owner-only.
- Classify every runtime export in HOST_EXPORTS as 'binds nothing'.
- Update README.md:306-307.
- No app calls it in this unit (tested but unreachable, per the #133 ruling).

ACCEPTANCE (tests/tunnel-device-registry.test.ts; all fail on main because the module is absent)
1. Mint through createDeviceCredentials over the registry, open a NEW registry on the same files (a restart), and `verify` returns the deviceId.
2. Revoke with a delete made to throw leaves the tombstone. A registry opened after a restart still refuses that credential.
3. A plain envelope with a sealer present, and a sealed envelope with no sealer, are both refused with a named error, and the file bytes are unchanged.
4. Group or other permission bits are refused, not tightened (reuse identity-store's checks, including macOS ACL).
5. An unknown version is refused.
6. The file bytes never contain the minted credential string or its secret half, only 32-byte digests and zero-byte tombstones. Decrypt the sealed envelope with the test sealer before searching.
7. Opening with a different bindTo reports 'binding-changed', and every old credential then fails verify.
8. Two concurrent mints both survive a restart.
9. list() exposes no digest field.

MUTATION CHECKS
- Persist no tombstone.
- Write the credential instead of its digest.
- Skip the mode check.
- Re-seal a plain file in place.
- Ignore bindTo.
- Drop the version check.
Each must fail.

- No socket.
- Nothing in apps/server/src imports it in this change. #249 requires the server statelessness correction in the same commit as the server's first use.
- Fail closed on every read error.

buildNow.name: BN8 Pairing exchange over pair frames, with the desktop's accept before any credential is minted
files: tests/layering.test.ts (seam regex at :1244 and entry-mapping checks at :708-738)

buildNow.brief:
WHY: nothing can pair. PairFrame.body is `unknown` ('Its shape is the exchange's to define', wire/index.ts:262-281), and the README lists the CPace messages, confirmation and credential handover as absent (packages/tunnel/README.md:315-318). The CPace steps (pake beginExchange :338, computeConfirmation :367, finish :397) and `channelIdentifierFor` (binding :104) have no production caller.

The #129 owner ruling (https://github.com/johnhenry/chatterang/issues/129#issuecomment-5668943416) says the desktop shows an accept prompt and mints only after acceptance, and a lapse spends the secret. But PAIRING_HANDOVER_MS = 10_000 (verified at host/index.ts:191) closes the claimant's channel before a person can answer. The prompt's length is an implementation constant to name and pin, as the owner said of the relayed-prompt timeout on #170 (https://github.com/johnhenry/chatterang/issues/170#issuecomment-5668943134), so it is settled here: `PAIRING_CONFIRM_MS = 60_000`. It is defined in exchange/ so host/index.ts gains no new runtime export and HOST_EXPORTS stays unchanged.

SCOPE: a platform-free new entry `@chatterang/tunnel/exchange`, using WebCrypto and noble through pake only.

It MUST NOT import host/, even type-only. Declare a structural `PairingAdmissionLike { claim(presented: Uint8Array): ClaimOutcome }` locally.

Initiator (phone) and responder (host) state machines over `pair` frame bodies:
1. Both sides contribute a sid share.
2. CPace messages with CI = channelIdentifierFor(route, negotiated SPKI).
3. Confirmation tags; `finish()` is the only path to a session key.
4. The responder sends 'awaiting-accept'.
5. The credential is sealed with AES-GCM under a key derived from the session key, or a named refusal is sent.

Gate mapping on the responder:
- A bad peer tag calls `admission.claim(<bytes that cannot match>)`, so the window's budget is spent (window.ts:221-241 decrements before the compare).
- A good tag calls `admission.claim(secret)`, which claims the window and ends the other pairing tunnels (host/index.ts:1105-1141).
- Then it awaits an injected `confirm({ route }): Promise<'accept' | 'decline'>` bounded by PAIRING_CONFIRM_MS, and mints through an injected `mint(window)` only on 'accept'.
- Decline or lapse cancels the window and closes the tunnel.

In host/index.ts, derive PAIRING_HANDOVER_MS from PAIRING_CONFIRM_MS plus a named mint margin.

No name step yet: what name the accept prompt shows is owner question 'Phone name'. Leave the step out; do not invent a placeholder field.

Layering:
- Ban the entry from src/ except the seam files (extend the TUNNEL_PAIRING regex at layering.test.ts:1244).
- Map it explicitly in tsconfig and vite, with no wildcard (layering :708-738).

ACCEPTANCE (tests/tunnel-exchange.test.ts, on a loopback createTunnelListener with tests/support/tunnel-gate.ts; all fail on main)
1. Scanned route, right token: confirm is called once. Accepting delivers a credential; reconnecting with TUNNEL_CREDENTIAL_HEADER is admitted as `{kind:'device'}`.
2. Accept at 30 s of injected clock still delivers. On main the 10 s handover closes the tunnel.
3. Typed route, five wrong codes: the window is exhausted and a sixth connection gets 401.
4. Decline: no mint (a spy), the window is cancelled, and a second phone is refused.
5. Lapse at PAIRING_CONFIRM_MS: identical to decline.
6. A negotiated SPKI different from the payload pin gives pin-mismatch before any pair frame on the scanned route, and a confirmation failure on the typed route.
7. No pair-frame body ever contains the credential string or either base64url half.
8. An out-of-order or oversized step ends the tunnel with PAIRING_ONLY limits (MAX_PAIRING_FRAME_BYTES 16384).

MUTATION CHECKS
- Mint before accept.
- Claim only on good tags, so a bad tag spends no budget.
- Send the credential unencrypted.
- Accept a second claim.
- Use an issuer-only sid.
- Restore the handover to 10 s.
Each must fail.

INVARIANTS
- pairing/ imports nothing.
- pake/ imports only noble.
- credential.ts semantics are unchanged.
- confirm never receives the secret.
- The phone half runs on WebCrypto only.
- The listen inventory is unchanged.

PROCESS
- Never use git stash; commit explicit paths; 'refs' only.
- Typecheck from a real checkout, not only a worktree: shared node_modules can resolve cross-package types to main's copy.

ownerQuestions.question: When your desktop runs a turn for your phone, may that turn ever go to a cloud provider the desktop is connected to (OpenAI and so on), for example because the desktop is hot, its model failed, or the phone picked a cloud model?

options.label: Never: desktop models only, no fallback (Recommended)
options.description: A phone turn runs only on models installed on the desktop. Heat or a failure becomes an error on the phone, never a silent switch to the cloud. The desktop's API keys are never loaded into the worker.

options.label: Only a cloud model the phone explicitly picks
options.description: The phone can choose one of the desktop's connected cloud models, and every tool-output send is asked on the phone. Still no silent fallback.

options.label: Allow the desktop's own fallback too
options.description: The desktop may divert a phone turn to its nominated cloud fallback. The phone is told afterwards, in the reply's label.

ownerQuestions.evidence:

- Your #7 ruling 2 says nothing about the phone's conversation is stored on the desktop, but does not address sending it onward.

ownerQuestions.question: You ruled that phone turns may use the tools the desktop allows for phones. What should those tools be able to reach on the desktop? Today the model's bash sees every desktop conversation under /chats, the folders you granted it, and commands that delete a model or open a chat. MCP calls normally remember a 'yes' per conversation.

options.label: Empty list by default; phone bash gets a fresh sandbox (Recommended)

options.label: Empty by default; phone bash sees what desktop bash sees
options.description: Same allowlist, but an allowed bash is the desktop's own shell, including /chats and granted folders. Every confirm is relayed to the phone.

options.label: No bash for phones in v1
options.description: Only MCP tools can be allowed for phones at first; each send is asked on the phone.
